# Guided AI GRC Build

**Proposal for Tamarack Instruments**
Prepared for Dana Whitfield, General Counsel

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. It has about 1,100 staff, and its AI maturity is at the piloting stage.

Three AI use cases are in scope:

- A customer service chatbot deployed on the support portal.
- An AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line.
- AI sales forecasting planned for next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. ISO/IEC 42001 work is to start next year, and its start date is not yet fixed.

Dana Whitfield has stated the objective directly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints apply:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

This proposal sets out a twelve-week guided build. It produces a functioning minimum viable Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) anchored on those three use cases. It responds to the June 2026 finding and organizes the work around ISO/IEC 42001 readiness themes.

## 2. The Case for a Guided Build

A conventional consulting engagement would deliver a finished governance pack and then leave. The Guided AI GRC Build works the other way. The Client's own team builds each artifact during the program, with weekly workshops, coaching and structured asynchronous work between sessions. At Week 12 the people who will operate the system are the people who wrote it. They understand why each control exists and can maintain it without depending on an outside party. This matters here for three reasons:

- **Inventory finding.** The inventory gap was raised as an internal audit finding, so the response has to be something the Client owns and can evidence over time.
- **Continuation into ISO/IEC 42001.** ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned for next year, and a system the Client already operates is a stronger starting point than documents it must first learn.
- **Operational depth.** Governing visual inspection on a production line requires judgment from quality, data, security and plant perspectives working together, and that judgment cannot be transferred in a handover file.

The program rests on three principles:

- **Slow AI** holds that AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit.
- **Informed Intent** holds that no AI system acts without prior authorization stating its purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, given by a human who meets the five authorizer conditions.
- **Final Liability rests with the Human** holds that every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene.

The program uses three frameworks:

- **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for the management system artifacts.
- **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for governed workflows and human oversight.
- **AI Governance for Boards** (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) as the reference for steering and board-layer reporting.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Inventory order.** The customer service chatbot enters the inventory first because it is the only deployed system and it operates on the customer-facing support portal. The visual inspection pilot enters second because it is the subject of the stated objective and sits on a production line, where the works council constraint applies. AI sales forecasting is recorded third as a planned system, so that it passes through intake governance before it is built rather than after.

| Week | Spine focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter scoped to the three named use cases. Named owner per system under Final Liability rests with the Human. Works council consultation plan logged as a delivery dependency. Evidence storage location agreed consistent with the EU data constraint. | Context of the organization; leadership; roles and authorities | Unknown |
| W2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot first, visual inspection second, sales forecasting as planned. Discovery of any further AI systems in use. | Scope of the AIMS; AI system records | June 2026 internal audit finding (no inventory of AI systems) |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology | Classification criteria covering EU AI Act categories and GDPR relevance, applied first to chatbot and visual inspection. Classification outcomes: confirm with external counsel. | Planning; AI risk assessment approach | Unknown |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments | Full assessments for chatbot and visual inspection. Scoping assessment for sales forecasting. | AI risk assessment; AI system impact assessment | Unknown |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment | Operating register populated from W4. Treatment owners named. | AI risk treatment | Unknown |
| W6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core policy set drafted for adoption, including the authorization standard under Informed Intent. | AI policy; leadership commitment | Unknown |
| W7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle stage gates, including the gate a pilot must pass before production, applied to visual inspection. | Operational planning and control; AI system life cycle | Unknown |
| W8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Supplier review for any third-party components behind the chatbot or visual inspection. Evidence collection starts. | Third-party relationships; documented information | Unknown |
| W9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Chatbot workflow governed end to end. Second workflow governed. Any element touching production staff held until works council consultation is complete. | Operation; use of AI systems; human oversight | Unknown |
| W10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring for chatbot responses. Evaluation criteria for the visual inspection pilot. | Performance evaluation; monitoring and measurement | Unknown |
| W11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change procedures. First review of four weeks of evidence. | Improvement; nonconformity and corrective action | Unknown |
| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Readiness review against the six-element definition. Evidence walkthrough with the build team. | Internal audit and management review readiness | Unknown |

**Integration points.** The Client operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. The program will attach AI governance to these structures rather than build parallel ones. Specific attachment points are marked `Unknown` until the relevant artifacts are confirmed at intake.

**Readiness, not certification.** The ISO/IEC 42001 mapping describes readiness themes only. The program does not certify, and it does not predict any certification, audit or regulatory outcome.

**Items with legal effect.** The following carry legal effect and must be confirmed with external counsel:

- EU AI Act classification of the chatbot and visual inspection systems.
- GDPR treatment of any personal data the systems process.
- The scope and timing of works council consultation.
- Data residency arrangements for customer data.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS comprising six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

Evidence collection starts in W8, which gives five weeks of collection by W12.

The chatbot is the deployed system and is the first candidate for a governed workflow. The second governed workflow is a question to confirm at intake. The program will not move the visual inspection pilot into production to satisfy this definition. Whether its pilot operation counts as production use for this purpose is also a question to confirm at intake.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

The build team is drawn from the following roles. The hours below are estimates per person per week, and they include the workshop, coaching and asynchronous work.

| Role | Estimated hours per week | Expected peak weeks |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 | W1, W3, W6, W12 |
| CISO | 4 to 6 | W8, W10, W11 |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 6 | W7, W9, W10 |
| Head of Data | 5 to 7 | W2, W3, W4, W10 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 4 | W4, W7, W9 |
| Internal auditors (two, each) | 2 to 3 | W2, W11, W12 |

The role of the two internal auditors is a question to confirm at intake. They could serve as contributors or as independent observers, and that choice affects their later independence when reviewing the system they helped build. Weekly coordination ownership is `Unknown` and is also confirmed at intake.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** confirms scope, team and decisions needed.
- **Week 6:** reviews spine status, blockers and any scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** receives the minimum viable AIMS attestation, an evidence sample index and a 12-month operating plan.

Steering reporting follows AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). Steering membership and any onward board reporting line are `Unknown` and are confirmed at intake.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format.** The program runs for 12 weeks. Each week includes one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions.

**Scheduling.** The start date is `Unknown`. Session scheduling across the Client's operating jurisdictions and the working language for sessions are confirmed at intake. Working materials and evidence storage will follow the requirement that customer data stays in the EU. The specific arrangement should be confirmed with external counsel.

**Price.** The price is US$60,000, which sits within the stated approval of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Whether the program dates fall within that fiscal year is a question to confirm at intake. Contract and payment terms will be set out in the engagement letter, and those terms should be confirmed with external counsel.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a 60-minute intake session before that date to confirm the following questions:

- Are there AI systems in use beyond the three named use cases, including AI features embedded in purchased software?
- Does the chatbot process personal or customer data, and where is it hosted?
- Does the visual inspection pilot capture images or data relating to production staff?
- Are third-party suppliers involved in the chatbot or visual inspection systems?
- Which ISMS, QMS and internal audit artifacts should AI governance attach to?
- Which workflow is the second governed workflow, and does pilot operation count as production use?
- What role will the two internal auditors take, and who coordinates the build team weekly?
- Who sits on the steering group, and is there a board reporting line?
- What is the preferred start date, and does it fall within the current fiscal year?

Answers to these questions finalize the W1 mobilization brief and allow the program to begin on the agreed date.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
